sources.title: SimuHome: A Temporal- and Environment-Aware Benchmark for Smart Home LLM Agents
sources.authors: Gyuhyeon Seo, Jungwoo Yang, Junseong Pyo, Nalim Kim, Jonggeun Lee, Yohan Jo
sources.use_in_aura: Supports executable goals, pre-action state checks, feasible/infeasible requests, device dependencies, and time-aware workflows.
sources.limits: The released benchmark is simulated and does not establish household authority rules or emergency policy. Aura does not copy its episodes.

sources.title: HomeBench: Evaluating LLMs in Smart Homes with Valid and Invalid Instructions Across Single and Multiple Devices
sources.authors: Silin Li, Yuhang Guo, Jiashu Yao, Zeming Liu, Haifeng Wang
sources.use_in_aura: Supports explicit invalid-request handling, mixed valid/invalid multi-device requests, and capability-aware evaluation.
sources.limits: Its instructions are generated in virtual homes and do not model mid-execution environmental changes.

sources.title: PersonalHomeBench: Evaluating Agents in Personalized Smart Homes
sources.use_in_aura: Supports paired single-factor counterfactuals, changed and unchanged answers, partial observability, and explicit physical and temporal consistency checks.
sources.limits: This source is a preprint and much of its household content is generated. It informs validation structure, not real-world frequencies.

sources.title: CASAS Smart Home Data Sets
sources.use_in_aura: Supports realistic room transitions, overlapping residents, longitudinal routines, and ambient sensor observations.
sources.limits: CASAS records activities and sensors; it does not provide normative smart-home control actions or priority rules.

sources.title: ARAS Human Activity Datasets in Multiple Homes with Multiple Residents
sources.authors: Hande Alemdar, Ozlem Durmaz Incel, Halil Ertan, Cem Ersoy
sources.use_in_aura: Supports simultaneous activities and state transitions for two residents in two real homes over two months.
sources.limits: ARAS is an activity-recognition dataset and does not encode device-control preferences or permissions.

sources.title: CASAS-SW Continuous In-the-wild Smartwatch Activity Data
sources.use_in_aura: Supports gaps, delayed labels, and last-observation-carried-forward behavior in real-world sensing traces.
sources.limits: The dataset uses wearable and location signals rather than Aura's exact ambient sensors; it supports the observation pathology, not a chosen delay duration.

sources.title: A perspective on multi-user interaction design based on an understanding of domestic lighting conflicts
sources.authors: Karin Niemantsverdriet, Harm van Essen, Berry Eggen
sources.use_in_aura: Supports activity and preference conflicts in shared lighting, including reading, sleeping, television viewing, brightness, and color-temperature differences.
sources.limits: The study warns against assuming one automatic resolution is socially correct. Aura scenarios must state the household agreement instead of inventing a universal winner.

sources.title: A User-Centric Evaluation of Smart Home Resolution Approaches for Conflicts Between Routines
sources.authors: Ali Zaidi, Rui Yang, Vinay Koshy, Camille Cobb, Indranil Gupta, Karrie Karahalios
sources.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies
sources.use_in_aura: Supports context-dependent routine conflicts and the need to evaluate more than one resolution strategy.
sources.limits: The study uses scenario surveys and finds no context-agnostic best policy; Aura must not encode a universal preference winner.

sources.title: NISTIR 8259A Federal Profile: Logical Access to Interfaces
sources.authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.use_in_aura: Supports role hierarchies, permitted device actions, unauthorized-interaction rejection, temporary roles, and least privilege.
sources.limits: This federal profile does not prescribe family-specific owner, adult, child, or guest precedence. Aura must declare those permissions in the household contract.

sources.title: SOTERIA: Automated IoT Safety and Security Analysis
sources.authors: Z. Berkay Celik, Patrick McDaniel, Gang Tan
sources.use_in_aura: Supports trace-level safety properties for smoke alarms and failures caused by interacting otherwise-safe automations.
sources.limits: It establishes that smoke detection must preserve alarm safety. It does not mandate Aura's exact lighting brightness or response window.

sources.title: Home, SafeHome: Ensuring a Safe and Reliable Home Using the Edge
sources.use_in_aura: Supports failures and disconnections during routines, concurrent command conflicts, and explicit safety invariants across device sequences.
sources.limits: Its motivating scenarios include device types Aura v1 does not model. Aura reuses the failure structure only where current device capabilities match.

sources.title: ARGUS: Context-Based Detection of Stealthy IoT Infiltration Attacks, accompanying dataset
sources.use_in_aura: Supports real device-state transitions across five homes, including three homes with four inhabitants.
sources.limits: The dataset targets intrusion detection and does not label benign device failures or prescribe recovery actions.

sources.title: From thermal comfort to conflict: The contested control and usage of domestic smart heating in the United Kingdom
sources.authors: Benjamin K. Sovacool, Mari Martiskainen, Jordan Osborn, Anaam Anaam, Matthew Lipson
sources.use_in_aura: Supports real household disagreement over temperature settings and heating practices in a 100-home living-lab study.
sources.limits: Observed conflict frequency and UK heating practices are not assumed to transfer unchanged to every Aura household.
